info.longBusinessSummary: Boku, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides local payment solutions for merchants in the Americas, the Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The company offers network of direct carrier billing, digital wallets, and account-to-account real-time payment schemes. It also provides additional value-added services, including currency conversion and cross-border funds settlement. The company provides its services through mobile network operators, digital wallets, cable TV companies, and others. Boku, Inc. was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in London, the United Kingdom.

rationale.growth: Years 1–2 from analyst consensus (9 analysts: 6.6%, 13.7%); then a straight-line fade to 2.5% terminal growth by year 7.
rationale.ebit_margin: Starts at last year's EBIT margin (15.4%) and moves to the 4-year median (10.8%) over 5 years.
rationale.tax: Median effective tax rate (24.4%), kept within 15–30%.
rationale.reinvestment: Historical medians: D&A 8.5%, capex 7.3% of revenue; working capital -30.0% of revenue, so each extra $1 of sales ties up $-0.30. Stock-based compensation (8.4% of revenue) stays inside GAAP EBIT and is not added back, so it is treated as a real cost. IFRS reporters: lease payments sit in financing cash flow, so check capex covers them.
rationale.wacc: CAPM: risk-free 4.91% (US 10-year Treasury yield (CBOE ^TNX via Yahoo Finance)) + adjusted beta 0.60 × ERP 5.0% + small-cap premium 1.0% = cost of equity 8.91%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.91% (interest ÷ debt). Market-value weights: debt 1.3%.
rationale.exit_multiple: Median peer EV/EBITDA (20.8x) as a cross-check terminal value.
